title: Holistic instrument design slate for multi-hop inference
content:
Purpose

This is a working slate to converge on an instrumentation and dashboard plan for multi-hop inference flows (multi-turn chat + tool calls + reranking + embedding lookups). Goal: a compact set of signals that help us detect: user-visible latency regressions, cost spikes tied to token inflation or inefficient KV reuse, traceable root cause to model/serving layer, and regressions in quality routing (fallbacks, model variants).

Scope & constraints
- Focus on hosted and dedicated execution paths initially; private deployments later.
- We need low-cardinality aggregates for live dashboards plus sparse rich traces for deep dives.
- Query budget: dashboards and synthetic probes must fit within the telemetry quota (target <12% additional query cost).
- Must be compatible with existing span/trace semantics (trace id per user request, spans for each model call, and sub-span for KV cache operations).

High-level proposal (summary)
- Core metrics: request-level latency (p50/p95/p99), tokenized cost per request, model-invocation-count, kv-cache-hit-rate (per-tenant and global), re-route/fallback-rate, prompt-amplification-ratio.
- Trace anchors: user request span -> routing span -> model invocation spans -> kv-cache spans -> postprocess spans. Each model span should include attributes: model_name, model_variant, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, quantization, batch_size, hardware_type, batch_wait_ms.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling tied to anomaly detection (more traces when cost/sli deviates) + static 0.1% baseline for coverage.
- Dashboard: an incident-first landing view (SLOs + recent anomalies) + ‘session replay’ pane showing multi-hop token flow and cache warmth visualization.

Detailed metric definitions (working; please comment)
- request.latency.ms: wall-clock time from API gateway entry to final response close. Dimensions: tenant_id, route, model_name, region, tier. Units: milliseconds. Aggregations: p50/p90/p95/p99, count.
- model.invocations.count: number of distinct inference calls kicked off during a request. Important for multi-hop. Dimensions: tenant, request_type (chat/api), driver (hosted/dedicated).
- token.cost.units: internal normalized token units used for billing-like visibility. Computed as sum(token_in + token_out * output_weight) across all invocations for request. Unit: token-units.
- prompt.amplification.ratio: (total_tokens_sent_to_models / original_user_tokens). Float >=1. Flags situations where system expands prompts (retrieval, summaries).
- kvcache.hit.rate: windowed hit rate for prefix/KV cache during request servicing. Dimensions: model_name, tenant, cold_start (bool). Definition: hits / (hits + misses) for requests in 1m window.
- fallback.rate: fraction of requests routed to a fallback model because of capacity or errors. Dimensions: fallback_reason (capacity, error, quality).
- batch.wait.ms: how long requests sit in a batch queue before execution. Important for balancing throughput vs latency.

Trace annotation schema (keeps span key-value pairs small):
- span.role: {proxy, router, allocator, model, kvcache, postprocess} 
- span.model: short model id (e.g., redwood/llama-2-70b-int8).
- span.seqlen.in: integer. span.seqlen.out: integer.
- span.kv.cacheable: boolean (true if request used prefix caching).
- span.kv.slot: small enum (global, tenant, route).
- span.qual.score: float (if postprocessing yields a quality scoring).
- span.reason.fallback: short enum if applicable (OOM, timeout, policy).

Practical tracing patterns
- Anchor one top-level trace per user request. Child spans for each model invocation so multi-hop flows are reconstructable. Include short token counts on spans to avoid large payloads.
- For chat sessions, emit periodic session-level markers (session.start, session.checkpoint) to allow grouping across traces for longer interactions.
- KV cache warmth: when cache hit rate drops below threshold use lightweight synthetic probe to ping prefixes and gather warmth metadata.

Dashboard layout (operator-first)
1) Incident landing (1 row):
   - SLOs (request.latency.p95 per-tenancy), error budget remaining, and a compact anomaly timeline (automatic).
2) Multi-hop heatmap (2 rows):
   - model.invocations.count per request distribution (histogram), prompt.amplification.ratio heatmap by route, average batch.wait.ms.
3) Cost attribution (2 rows):
   - token.cost.units per-tenant with model breakdown, token churn (tokens produced then fed back in), and per-request cost boxplot.
4) KV cache panel (1 row):
   - kvcache.hit.rate, slot-level warmth, cache evictions over time, cold-start signals.
5) Tracing quickcards (1 row):
   - top 5 recent high-latency traces with span waterfall, top fallback reasons, and quick-link to trace viewer with pre-filtered attributes.
6) Quality fencing (1 row):
   - fallback.rate over time, model variant rollback triggers, and a simple quality-signal (qual.score median) with alerts if it changes by >5%.

Sampling & cost-control
- Baseline: 0.1% uniformly sampled traces for long-run coverage.
- Escalation: if p95 latency increases >15% vs daily baseline or token.cost.units bursts by >2x then temporarily escalate sampling for the affected tenant/route to 5% for 30 minutes.
- Auto-truncate large attributes (token streams) in traces and keep only lengths and hashes. Avoid storing raw prompts in traces unless explicit opt-in.

Ownership and rollout plan (short)
- Owners: Observability core (Asha), Serving Runtime (Diego) for model span attributes, Platform Routing (Priya) for routing spans, SRE (Evan) for dashboard ops.
- Milestones:
  - Week 0–2: finalize metric defs and trace schema; PR to telemetry repo for new tags. (owner: Asha)
  - Week 3–4: backend instrumentation (model spans + kv cache spans) on staging; add enrichment for seq_len and batch_wait. (owners: Diego + Priya)
  - Week 5: sampling policies + anomaly-trigger test (synthetic). (owner: SRE)
  - Week 6: dashboard wireframes + alpha panels; internal dogfood.

Open questions / tradeoffs (please add):
- Should token.cost.units be billed-weighted (mirror billing) or simplified normalized units for observability? Pros/cons: fidelity vs cardinality.
- How much session-level context should we retain for private deployments? (privacy and retention constraints).
- Are we comfortable with probabilistic sampling tied to anomaly detectors (adds complexity to inference of rates)?

Immediate TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Diego: draft small change set to add span.seqlen.* and span.kv.slot attributes to model-span (due 2025-11-28).
- [ ] Priya: sketch dashboard wireframe in Looker/Grafana; include a session replay mock for multi-hop (due 2025-12-04).
- [ ] Evan: prototype sampling escalation rule in staging with synthetic spike. (due 2025-12-11).
- [ ] All: review metric defs above and comment inline in Confluence page (link in linked_artifacts).

Notes to self / heuristics captured here
- Keep the live landing page to <8 widgets to reduce cognitive overhead.
- Favor derived low-cardinality signals for alerting but keep high-cardinality flavor for exploratory panels (tenant/model breakdowns).
- Treat prompt amplification as a first-class signal for cost regressions — it's often invisible in raw invocation counts.

Recent references and context snippets
- See confluence: Multi-hop Inference Background for experiments on synthetic chat storms that produced huge prompt amplification (link above).
- GH PR 127 contains earlier telemetry schema attempts; new schema tries to shrink attribute set while keeping investigability.
